#5008. Crypto crash ahead? Why the next TWO weeks could rattle markets

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The next two weeks could be crucial for investors.

The macroeconomic calendar has several important data releases this week, with the October PCE Inflation report on Wednesday being the most significant. With only two weeks until the next FOMC meeting, these releases may have an impact on market expectations for the Fed’s next potential rate move. However, investor positioning already suggests that crypto assets remain vulnerable.

Investor Bill Ackman said in a post on X that given increased spending on AI technologies and increased borrowing costs at SpaceX (now at 8.259%, compared to less than 6% pre-IPO), a 3% inflation target may be a more realistic target than 2% as set by the Federal Reserve.

In addition, Elon Musk also raised concerns around the increasing cost of components (chips, energy, data centers, etc.) in AI systems, and how this is putting pressure on company balance sheets, reinforcing concerns that AI may cause prolonged inflationary pressures.

In this light, markets are still leaning towards the Fed holding rates at the upcoming FOMC meeting, even if October’s inflation data comes in hotter than expected. However, some investors believe rate hikes are already being priced in as a way to cool the AI boom and curb rising valuations.

Naturally, such uncertainty in Fed policy is putting more pressure on crypto markets. As such, given that risk appetite is also low, the question is whether a year-end crypto crash is becoming a bigger possibility.

Over the last 48 hours, the U.S. market has seen significant selling pressure.

The sell-off has triggered a broad de-risking across equities, metals, and crypto, wiping out trillions in market value. U.S. equities alone have shed $5.5 trillion in market cap, while the crypto market has lost around $2.2 trillion. Bitcoin [BTC] slipped below $56k as selling pressure spread across the market.

Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump warned that things “will only get worse,” blaming Democratic midterm election wins for wiping out nearly $6 trillion in stock market value since the election. However, investors aren’t entirely buying this explanation. Instead, concerns around Fed policy, sticky inflation, and the rising U.S. debt ceiling are increasingly driving market fears.

The result? Some investors now see the possibility of further rate hikes as a “deliberate” move to cool an overheated market.

This relates to the debate around the likely decision of the Fed. While some are concerned that further interest rate rises may cause a recession within the economy, others believe tighter monetary conditions are required to put inflated market values back into line.

In this scenario, the next two weeks could prove crucial for crypto markets. With AI bubble concerns building, major macro data ahead, Trump’s latest warning, and growing uncertainty around the Fed’s next move, crypto’s recent dip could be the start of a much broader correction.

Seven key macro releases, rising AI costs, and uncertainty around the Fed’s next move could keep crypto markets under pressure.

A $5.5 trillion U.S. market wipeout, Trump’s warning, and growing rate hike fears raise the risk of a deeper crypto correction over the next two weeks.

#5006. Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit has produced an estimated $5.7 million in losses across two stages, according to SlowMist’s incident tracker. After unbacked ACE tokens were minted on BNB Chain and sold, traders reportedly used the resulting price collapse to withdraw real ACE from the project’s Endurance bridge reserves. The fallout reached centralized exchanges on Monday, November 23: Bithumb halted ACE trading after finding indications that abnormally issued tokens had entered crypto exchanges.

This was not one attacker walking away with $5.7 million in a single transaction. The distinction matters. Roughly $1.87 million was traced through the attacker’s proceeds, while another 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued around $3.7 million at the incident’s reference prices, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. SlowMist lists a combined $5.7 million loss estimate, not an audited final total. The bridge’s most basic promise, that a token issued on one chain corresponds to something real on another, is precisely what now needs proving.

Security firm Blockaid flagged the Fusionist bridge-minter exploit on November 22. Its alert described the mechanism bluntly:

A privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT.

The firm initially estimated that about $1.04 million had been extracted while the attack was still ongoing. That was an interim snapshot, not a cap on the damage.

Blockchain-monitoring account Onchain Lens subsequently reported that an attacker had routed 1,091.5 ETH, valued at about $1.87 million at the time, through Tornado Cash. That observation traces a movement of proceeds, not an extra $1.87 million to add on top of the initial extraction estimate. The values describe different points in the same suspected attacker’s fund flow.

Fusionist acknowledged an apparent ongoing ACE exploit on BNB Smart Chain on Sunday and asked users to suspend transfers, trading and bridging on that network. It has not, in the material reviewed, provided a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem identifying how the privileged minting authority was abused.

A bridge minter is supposed to create a token representation only when the corresponding value is properly accounted for. Once the right to mint is misused, a chain can show perfectly ordinary-looking balances that have no matching backing.

It is a familiar failure mode: NewsBTC previously covered a bridge-role exploit that minted unbacked tokens at CrediX. That earlier case does not establish Fusionist’s root cause, but it illustrates why elevated bridge permissions are such a consequential security boundary.

The subsequent drain may prove more important than the initial minting spree.

According to SlowMist’s November 22 incident entry, traders bought the sharply discounted ACE created by the market disruption and used the cross-chain bridge to withdraw about 53.7 million genuine ACE from the Endurance-side reserves. SlowMist valued that withdrawal at approximately $3.7 million.

Here is the mechanism without the jargon. A representation of ACE on BNB Chain suddenly became cheap because unauthorized supply had flooded the market. A bridge that would still accept those tokens in exchange for ACE on Endurance offered an obvious difference in value.

Anyone able to complete that conversion could receive real tokens in return for deeply discounted ones. The trading opportunity existed because the backing and the circulating representation were no longer in a trustworthy relationship.

The $3.7 million figure is a valuation of the ACE reserve outflow, not proof that every recipient sold those tokens for $3.7 million in cash. Nor does it mean every trader involved helped compromise the minter.

There is a meaningful difference between initiating the security breach and trading through a system whose defenses have already failed.

Those distinctions should not obscure the core problem. A bridge can have technically valid transactions and still produce an economically disastrous result. If unbacked supply can be redeemed for genuine reserves, the checks have failed where they matter most.

Bithumb suspended ACE deposits and withdrawals early on November 23. It then halted trading effective 7:30 a.m. Korea time, according to its follow-up ACE security notice.

The exchange said, in a translation from its Korean announcement, that it had:

confirmed indications that abnormally issued ACE had entered cryptocurrency exchanges.

It identified two related BNB Chain transactions and a second transaction.

Those records are important evidence leads, but a full independent decoding of the transaction trail remains outstanding.

Bithumb’s wording is careful: it reported signs of abnormal supply entering exchanges, not a finding that every ACE token in customer accounts is invalid. The trading suspension is a protective response, not a finalized determination of customer losses.

Still, it creates a practical problem for holders who never used the bridge. If tokens are fungible within a market, exchanges and the issuer need a credible method for identifying affected supply and deciding how deposits, balances and trades will be treated.

There is an understandable temptation to focus on the enormous minting figures. The more consequential question is what happened when those tokens met the bridge’s reserves.

A system does not need to lose control of its entire blockchain to suffer a serious failure in one privileged contract role. Nor should a successful-looking bridge transaction count as evidence that the asset being transferred was fully backed.

The response cannot end with a pause notice and a promise to investigate.

Fusionist needs to show which minting permissions were affected, whether they have been revoked, how much ACE was created without backing, how the Endurance-side reserve changed and what claims remain outstanding.

Exchanges need a defensible token-treatment plan, and holders need to know whether there is a shortfall and who is responsible for covering it.

There is a fair counterargument: the $5.7 million figure is an external estimate, market prices moved during the incident, and the precise compromise method is not established.

SlowMist categorizes the incident as private-key leakage, but that classification is not a substitute for an official technical finding. It would also be premature to treat a cautious exchange halt as proof that every affected customer suffered a loss.

Those qualifications change how the numbers should be reported. They do not make the underlying bridge-accounting failure less serious.

The next credible milestone is not a restored interface or a reassuring social post. It is a transparent reconciliation of the tokens minted, the reserves withdrawn and the assets still available to back legitimate ACE claims.

Until that exists, the estimated $5.7 million fallout remains a warning about both token security and the risks of trusting a bridge’s accounting.

#5005. XRP’s Below $1 Not For Long? Supply Tightens

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP’s Below $1 Not For Long? Supply Tightens

XRP has slipped below the $1 mark even as the amount available on Binance is tightening sharply.

XRP has fallen below the $1 level even as available supply on Binance appears to be shrinking, leaving the token between constrained exchange inventory and a lack of fresh institutional buying.

Recent reports put XRP near $0.95 after a steep monthly decline, with the token briefly trading under $0.90 during November’s broader sell-off. Intermittent rebounds have occurred, but price has not yet established a durable hold above the $1 mark.

US spot XRP ETFs have gone through their longest stretch without a net inflow since launch, according to SoSoValue data. The funds last recorded an $8.43 million net inflow on October 29 and have since seen roughly $26 million in withdrawals, though flows on November 18 and 19 were described as flat rather than net negative.

The pause matters because ETF buyers had previously provided incremental demand. Total net assets in the funds stood at about $1.08 billion by November 19, down from roughly $1.77 billion in late September, while cumulative inflows since launch remained near $1.8 billion.

XRP’s price action reflects that gap. The token was down about 3.6% over one recent seven-day period and roughly 28% over the prior month in another snapshot. Its 30-day Sharpe ratio was reported near negative 0.41, indicating that recent returns have not compensated for the asset’s volatility.

CryptoQuant’s XRP Supply Shortage Index for Binance rose to 2.4 on November 19, above its July reading of 2.09. Readings above 2 are described as severe tightness, and net withdrawals from the exchange exceeded $127 million between November 10 and 16.

Lower exchange balances can reduce immediately available selling inventory, but they do not form a standalone bullish signal. One analyst noted that part of the movement could reflect internal Binance reserve management rather than accumulation by long-term holders.

XRP’s price action has not yet confirmed stronger demand. XRP remains below its 200-day moving average, sitting very near $1.26, and repeated closes below $1 have turned that former support into nearby resistance.

Traders are watching the $0.94 area first, followed by support around $0.88. A sustained break below the latter could open a path toward $0.80, while a recovery would need to reclaim roughly $0.985 and then $1 before a broader reversal appears more credible.

The more relevant signal for the market is whether ETF flows resume as Bitcoin and broader risk sentiment stabilize. Tighter supply can amplify a move higher, but without returning demand it can also coexist with a fragile price floor.

Pump.fun [PUMP] is up 4.74% over the past 24 hours as of writing, a slightly more positive gain compared to the rest of the crypto market, which rose 2.34%. While there is no verified catalyst behind the rally, PUMP’s reported cross-margin and Pro mode rollout may have sparked interest in the token again. Furthermore, the broader market’s recovery and a bid-heavy order book could be another reason for the surge.

However, the recent rally is looking cautiously optimistic, as the recovery is yet to overcome the bearish trend, leaving PUMP at considerable risk of another pullback in the near term.

On the daily chart, PUMP was trading at $0.002568 at the time of writing and approaching the 23.6% Fibonacci resistance at $0.002745. However, the broader price structure remains firmly bearish, with the token continuing to make lower highs and lower lows.

Reclaiming this Fibonacci level would be an initial sign that buyers are gaining ground, but the chances of that happening in the near term appear to be slim to none.

The indicators were also pointing to a potential near-term reversal with an RSI of 31.53 and OBV continuing its downtrend, indicating that sellers are still in control of the market. This makes it difficult for the recent price recovery to develop into a sustained reversal.

The four-hour chart offered a slightly more encouraging picture. After recovering over the past two days, PUMP reclaimed the 61.8% Fibonacci level at $0.002554 and entered the golden pocket. However, it has since started to retest the support, making this an important area to defend. Holding above it could open the door to $0.002654, the next Fibonacci resistance.

The MACD showed improving momentum, with its line above the signal line, although both remained below zero. H4 OBV also maintained its broader upward trend despite a recent dip, suggesting buying interest had eased slightly.

It’s absolutely vital that the bulls defend $0.002554 successfully, as it would extend the recovery toward $0.002745. Losing this support, on the other hand, would expose $0.002484 and potentially further losses.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has softened the tone of his recent Bitcoin warnings and said on X that the cryptocurrency held at the level it needed to hold after its drop to $55,150 over the weekend.

"Bitcoin held exactly where it had to hold -- for now anyway, but perhaps for more than now," Brandt wrote on Monday.

Brandt also shared a monthly chart of Bitcoin together with the post. The chart goes back to 2018, and Brandt marked on it the same patterns that he had already pointed to in previous years. According to the chart, the price of Bitcoin was back above $63,000 at the time of the post and stood at $63,338.

On Saturday, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150. It was the lowest price of the cryptocurrency since September 2024, and before that, the lowest price of Bitcoin in 2026 was $57,718 on July 1, according to Coinbase.

On Nov. 15, Brandt posted a weekly chart with a possible head-and-shoulders top and said that, if the pattern proves valid, Bitcoin's October 2025 record of about $126,000 may not be surpassed in his lifetime. Two days before that, on Nov. 13, Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August.

Brandt has also pointed to the history of Bitcoin's bull market cycles more than once. Late last year, he posted a chart showing that each of Bitcoin's five major bull runs began after drawdowns of 75% or more, and he wrote that if the decline carried to $50,000, "the next bull market cycle should carry to $200k to $250K."

In April, Brandt said that Bitcoin could form an "investable low" in September or October 2026. According to Brandt, this low may or may not go below the February low near $60,000, and the next cycle peak could land between $300,000 and $500,000 in September or October 2029 if the four-year cycle continues to hold.

"Real bottom will not occur until October 2026," Brandt said in an interview in February.

The latest Brandt post comes amid a rally in U.S. tech stocks on Monday. Earlier that day, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately.

According to the Nvidia announcement, the board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government before the decision, and it is confident that Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Shares of Nvidia surged 33% after the news, according to CNBC.

Bitcoin went up together with tech stocks and briefly climbed above $64,000 on Monday. Before the Nvidia news, Bitcoin had already recovered from the Saturday low to around $61,500.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12. On Nov. 17, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said on the company's earnings call that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

#5002. Bitcoin Hits $63K on Nvidia News—Could It Be a Trap?

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Hits $63K on Nvidia News—Could It Be a Trap?

Risk appetite returned in force on Monday—but big players aren’t acting like the bottom is in.

Bitcoin price climbed approximately 4% to around $63,200 on November 23, staging a sharp recovery after plunging to a Saturday low of $55,081 over the weekend.

The rebound followed a sudden turnaround in U.S. tech equities and a wave of forced liquidations across crypto derivatives markets.

US markets staged a sharp rebound on Monday, November 23, led by a stunning 26% surge in Nvidia (NVDA) shares, after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil

The move helped reverse the recent tech and AI sell-off, sending Nasdaq 100 futures up 3.1% and S&P 500 futures up 2.4%, lifting risk appetite across global markets, including crypto.

Bitcoin price recovery was further amplified by a short squeeze. More than $440 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $370.2 million in shorts. Bitcoin short liquidations alone accounted for $172.91 million, according to CoinGlass.

Despite Monday’s bounce, underlying institutional data reveals ongoing caution. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $669.16 million in net outflows on Friday—their largest single-day capital exit since June 25, according to SoSoValue.

Over the past week, spot Bitcoin ETFs lost roughly $1.8 billion, marking their fourth consecutive week of net outflows.

Corporate accumulation also showed signs of restraint. Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, purchased 457 BTC for $28 million last week—a modest addition compared to the $212 million it spent repurchasing its own STRC stock over the same period.

“The biggest Bitcoin corporate holder isn’t capitalizing on the dip,” crypto investor Ted Pillows noted on X.

Market analysts remain divided on whether the weekend drop marked a final floor or a temporary pause before another leg down.

Prominent trader Astronomer (@Astronomer_zero) suggested on X that while Bitcoin approached a macro bottom near the $56,000 level over the weekend, the current move to $63,200 is likely a relief bounce rather than a confirmed bottom, warning that a downward retrace remains probable.

$btc 56k bottom looking really good now, with a 10%+ bounce so far.Even though I think this will retrace and I deem it just a bounce, it is a very important bounce and a strong bounce like this has significance and is exactly what we wanted to see.If you remember my short… https://t.co/TzN9MxF9tc pic.twitter.com/WitozYCG5Z

However, the trader argues that a durable bottom is forming soon and expects Bitcoin to hold above $50,000.

His thesis centers on Bitcoin’s estimated electricity production cost—currently around $60,300—which has historically served as a reliable long-term accumulation zone during cycles in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2026.

When prices dip below mining electricity costs, inefficient miners shut down, network difficulty adjusts downward, and supply pressure eases, establishing a technical and economic floor near $50,000.

#5001. Trump’s Meme Coin Dinner Exposes a 94% Collapse in Holder Commitments

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Donald Trump’s latest meme coin dinner came with a striking financial comparison: wallets displayed on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held approximately $9.1 million in tokens at the November 16 cutoff, compared with roughly $148 million associated with the first dinner in May 2025. That puts the decline in the publicly measured dollar value at close to 94%. It does not mean investors withdrew 94% of their cash, or that 94% fewer people turned up for dinner.

Trump hosted the third event for major $TRUMP holders at his Virginia golf club on Sunday, November 22. The gathering itself was new, but the more interesting story is what the leaderboard reveals about a token that was once able to turn a private invitation into a market-wide buying contest. NewsBTC previously covered an earlier $TRUMP meme coin dinner rally. This time, the numbers tell a considerably less flattering story about the value attached to that privilege.

The roughly $9.1 million estimate comes from Public Citizen’s November 22 review of the 130 wallets displayed on the final public leaderboard. Its researchers counted 9,794,832.87 $TRUMP tokens and valued them at approximately $0.93 each at the November 16, 9 a.m. Eastern cutoff. The older $148 million comparison refers to the first gala’s leaderboard in May 2025.

Source: Official $TRUMP Gala Dinner Leaderboard (November 16, 2026). Rankings based on time-weighted token holdings. Wallet entries do not necessarily represent individual attendees.

That works out to a decline of roughly 93.9%, rounded to 94%. But the events did not have identical leaderboard sizes or necessarily identical valuation methods. More importantly, the token’s price fell dramatically between the two events. A lower marked-to-market balance can reflect falling prices even if some holders retain comparable token quantities.

Calling this a 94% collapse in new investment would therefore be wrong. The narrower conclusion is still hard to ignore: the value represented by the public competition for dinner access is a small fraction of what it was at the first event.

The leaderboard also should not be mistaken for a headcount. While the public display showed 130 wallets, organizers said 185 wallets qualified under the event’s rules. One person can control multiple wallets, and a wallet can be held for an organization. Neither figure identifies exactly who attended Sunday night’s dinner.

The smaller overall value is only part of the picture. Public Citizen found that the top 10 wallets held about 81% of the tokens on the public board. The top 29 accounted for approximately 95%. Those top-ranked wallets were also eligible for a special VIP reception.

The concentration matters because a leaderboard is marketed as a contest between investors, but its aggregate value can be dominated by a very small number of positions. Looking at the $9.1 million as if it represented broad, evenly distributed enthusiasm would be as misleading as treating all 130 wallet entries as separate people.

There is a revealing detail near the bottom of Public Citizen’s review: the wallet ranked No. 130 held only 9.71 $TRUMP, worth about $9 at the snapshot. It qualified because the competition measured time-weighted holdings over the scoring period, rather than the balance left in the wallet at the very end. That is perfectly compatible with the rules. It also shows why a dinner ranking cannot be read as a simple list of fresh purchases or long-term conviction.

There is another market point here. A buyer who wants dinner access can acquire the token and hedge some of the price risk elsewhere. Holding a spot position long enough to earn a place does not necessarily make someone a directional believer in the coin. In that sense, the competition measures an incentive to qualify, not a clean vote of confidence in future returns.

Public Citizen’s researchers traced 66 of the 130 displayed wallets, or 51%, to direct transfers from exchanges that restrict US customers. Those wallets represented about 4.35 million $TRUMP, roughly 44% of the public board’s token holdings. Among the top 29 VIP-ranked wallets, 15 had received tokens directly from such exchanges, according to the group’s November 22 findings.

That is useful on-chain information. It is not proof that 66 dinner guests were foreign nationals, that all those exchanges served prohibited customers, or that any particular attendee broke a rule. An exchange withdrawal identifies a source of tokens, not a passport or the identity of the person controlling the receiving wallet. Public Citizen put a basic transparency problem plainly: “The names of the invitees have not been disclosed.” That sentence matters because a wallet address, however transparent its transaction history, cannot supply the accountability that a named guest list would provide.

GetTrumpMemes.com is not political and has nothing to do with any political campaign or any political office or governmental agency.

That is the organizers’ characterization. It does not remove the transparency question created when holders of a president-linked digital asset can compete for personal access to the president. Neither does that question, by itself, prove an improper exchange of favors.

There is a credible bullish counterargument. An exclusive dinner is a limited, experience driven reward. Its value to attendees need not move in lockstep with the coin’s market capitalization, and falling token prices can make it cheaper for new participants to qualify. The gala went ahead, and its promoters continue to offer other experiences to holders.

But that is precisely why we should be careful about treating an invitation contest as evidence of a durable investment base. Access is an incentive. It is not a claim on business earnings, and it does not put a floor under the price of the coin.

The most uncomfortable part of this comparison for $TRUMP holders is not that the dinner was smaller or less glamorous. The available figures do not establish either claim. It is that the token’s most recognizable promotional feature remains personal access, while the dollar value visible on the public leaderboard has fallen dramatically since the first event.

In our view, that weakens the argument that repeated celebrity events, by themselves, can sustain the market’s appetite for the token. A more persuasive sign of recovering demand would be durable, independently observable holdings beyond a contest period, with less dependence on a few top-ranked wallets. The next useful data would be post-event wallet balances and exchange flows, measured against the November 16 snapshot, not just another photograph from the dinner.

For now, the 94% comparison is a warning about the dollar value of the visible leaderboard, not proof of a 94% investor exodus. That distinction makes the story more credible, and no less troubling for anyone relying on the dinner promotion as an investment thesis.

#4999. Bitcoin Bloodbath Fails to Stop Michael Saylor's Buying Spree

Despite the sharp fall in the cryptocurrency market, Michael Saylor-led Strategy has not stopped its Bitcoin (BTC) buying spree, as it picked up 457 BTC worth around $29.6 million.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

The latest data from Strategy's SEC filing reveals that the firm has bought 457 Bitcoin at an average price of $64,898 per coin.

The new purchase brings Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings to around 851,305 BTC, which accounts for over 4% of the cryptocurrency's maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The firm has now spent around $64.23 billion to build its Bitcoin holdings at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin.

It is worth noting that Strategy has been buying BTC at gradually decreasing prices as the cryptocurrency market continues to bleed heavily.

On Nov. 2, the firm announced that it had bought 811 BTC, worth around $65.5 million, at an average price of $80,846 per Bitcoin.

A week later, on Nov. 9, Strategy announced the purchase of 1,036 BTC worth $81.9 million at an average price of $79,012.

The firm’s Bitcoin purchase a week later, on Nov. 16, was relatively smaller at 485 BTC, worth $33.4 million, with an average price of $68,887.

The new 457 BTC purchase continues this pattern. The latest Strategy purchase was made at an almost 20% lower price than the firm’s Nov. 2 acquisition.

Overall, the firm has made four weekly purchases, scooping up around 2,789 BTC worth $210.4 million.

However, these purchases have been much smaller than before. The latest $29.6 million purchase is almost 64% lower than the $81.9 million purchase announced just two weeks ago.

Although Saylor is doubling down on Bitcoin, Strategy’s massive holdings in the cryptocurrency are underwater as the market has been struggling to regain its footing.

On Nov. 21, Bitcoin hit a low of around $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, before rebounding above $61,000.

The firm’s recent purchases have helped reduce its overall average Bitcoin acquisition cost, but the drop has not been that significant.

For example, with the latest purchase, the average cost of the firm’s Bitcoin holdings dropped from $75,452 to around $75,446, a decline of just $6 per Bitcoin.

At the same time, the firm has also been putting a lot of resources into supporting its preferred securities.

In the latest reporting period, Strategy sold around 1.93 million common shares, raising net proceeds of $176.7 million.

#4998. Bitcoin rockets above $64,000 as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang, wiping out $372 million in shorts

Nearly 92% of the $404 million liquidated across crypto markets in one hour came from bearish bets caught by the sudden reversal.

Bitcoin jumped more than 4% in an hour to $64,427 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday.

The sudden rally triggered $424 million in crypto market liquidations within an hour, according to CoinGlass, as traders betting on further declines were caught by the price reversal.

CoinGlass rolling one-hour snapshot supplied November 23, 2026. Liquidated position values, not traders' realized net losses. Longs and shorts sum to $424.95 million; shorts account for about 88.7%. Screenshot capture time is not displayed. Later live dashboard readings can differ.

Source: CoinGlass liquidation dashboard, supplied November 23, 2026 one-hour screenshot

Short positions accounted for $376 million, or 92.2% of the liquidations, while bullish traders lost $31.58 million.

Bitcoin led the losses with $188 million in liquidations, 95.6% of which came from short positions. Ethereum followed with around $80 million, with shorts accounting for 92.9%.

Source: CoinGlass liquidation dashboard, supplied November 23, 2026 one-hour screenshot

Together, the two largest cryptocurrencies accounted for nearly 64% of the $403.98 million liquidated during the hour.

The concentration of short liquidations suggests that forced position closures amplified Bitcoin's initial rally, accelerating its recovery from last week's selloff.

That decline had briefly pushed Bitcoin below $60,000 following Huang's abrupt departure from Nvidia on Nov. 12, which triggered turmoil across technology stocks and added pressure to an already struggling crypto market.

Monday's reversal also lifted Nvidia shares by roughly 33% to around $170 in premarket trading, reversing part of the losses accumulated during the leadership crisis.

Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang marks a dramatic reversal from its position last week, when board Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out bringing the company's co-founder back as chief executive.

The board voted Monday unanimously to restore Huang as president, CEO, and a director after discussions that satisfied members about his candor and ability to lead the company.

Nvidia also said senior US government officials provided input during the deliberations, giving directors confidence that Huang's return posed no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”

Huang's return followed mounting pressure from shareholders, technology executives and President Donald Trump, who had publicly supported reinstating the Nvidia co-founder.

Strive CEO Matt Cole welcomed the decision, saying Nvidia was the largest single holding among Strive Asset Management's clients, with nearly $100 million invested through its ETFs.

Cole said Strive had prepared to submit a shareholder proposal requesting an advisory vote on Huang's reinstatement before Monday's market opening, but the board acted before the proposal became necessary.

Huang, who had previously expressed willingness to return, said he was honored to resume leadership of the company. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will return to her previous responsibilities.

However, Huang's reinstatement does not end the investigation into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

Nvidia said its independent board committee would complete that investigation while a newly established national security and export control committee oversees trade compliance and related risks.

The company is also recruiting a chief compliance officer and will continue cooperating with government investigations.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin's rapid recovery marks its second sharp Nvidia-linked rally within a week.

The cryptocurrency briefly reached approximately $64,600 following Nvidia's stronger-than-expected earnings last week, only to surrender most of those gains within 35 minutes.

Monday's advance returned Bitcoin to within roughly $173 of that previous high, with more than $372 million in forced short closures accompanying the move.

Analyst Zach Rector says he has nearly exhausted his buying funds after adding to positions below $1, while projecting a recovery toward $7 – $10. His argument rests on previous market cycles and a claimed record-low monthly momentum reading, not a confirmed catalyst for a rebound.

Previous rallies do not establish a floor. The analyst acknowledged that XRP could still fall toward $0.70 – $0.80 if geopolitical tensions trigger further market selling.

Beyond the initial recovery target, the host suggested institutional utility could eventually support prices of $20 – $30. #4995. XRP Briefly Tops $1 as Short Squeeze Hits 578% Liquidation Imbalance

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

On Monday, XRP briefly rose above $1 after the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia sparked a rally on Wall Street and a wave of short liquidations in the crypto market. At the peak of the move, short liquidations on XRP exceeded long liquidations by 578%, according to CoinGlass data.

On the XRPUSDT perpetual contract on Binance, the price of XRP went from $0.94 to as high as $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, and later it pulled back and stood at $0.984, according to TradingView.

Earlier on Monday, before the opening bell, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The company said that the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings with him, and that its independent investigation would continue. According to the company, the board received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk."

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and on Nov. 17, during the company's earnings call, Jones said that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

In premarket trading, Nvidia stock jumped 27% to $159.48 as of 9 a.m. ET, and at the start of U.S. trading on Monday, Nvidia shares were up more than 30%. The rally spread across Wall Street, and the S&P 500 rose as much as 5.6% and the Nasdaq 100 as much as 7.9%, according to NBC News.

CoinGlass data shows that $9.45 million worth of XRP positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and $7.18 million of that amount came from short positions. Long positions accounted for $2.27 million.

The same happened across the rest of the crypto market. In total, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, and shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

Bitcoin led the list with $273.26 million in liquidations, and 82.8% of that amount came from short positions. Ethereum followed with $139.07 million, and Solana was third with $24.93 million.

Besides, perpetual contracts on Nvidia stock and on SOXL, a triple-leveraged exchange-traded fund on semiconductor stocks, were next on the list with $16.34 million and $15.01 million in liquidations, respectively, according to CoinGlass.

#4994. Bitcoin drops to $55K after $670M liquidations – What changes now?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Last week, Bitcoin [BTC] fell to a low of $55,130 on Saturday, the 20th of November. This was lower than $57,800, which the leading crypto registered on the 1st of July.

It led to debate around whether the bear market was truly over, or whether what we saw in August-September was only a pause within the longer-term bearish trend.

Over the past two weeks, Bitcoin liquidations exceeded $600 million on four separate days.

The 11th and the 20th of November, when BTC breached key support levels at $73k and $61.4k, saw the heaviest long liquidations. Also, contextually speaking, these two days witnessed $690 million and $670 million in long liquidations, respectively.

The persistent downward price action was accompanied by relentless selling. Since the 5th of November, every trading day bar one has seen negative spot ETF flows.

Last week’s net outflows alone reached $1.245 billion. This incessant selling would need to ease before Bitcoin could find room to recover.

As things stand, a weekly trading session close below $57,800 is needed to flip the structure bearishly. The previous week’s correction, though deep, might be just a liquidity sweep before a recovery.

Bitcoin holders are under severe strain as prices approach or drop below their cost basis, and Open Interest has plunged dramatically. It was a result of tightening monetary policy and the global equity market downturn.

Over the past year, the BTC Open Interest was down by $4.5 billion.

In July, this figure fell as low as $6.5 billion. It was the largest OI downturn in Bitcoin’s history in dollar terms, observed crypto analyst Darkfost.

There have been eight trading days in 2026 with over $1.5 billion in liquidations across the crypto market. A decline in risk appetite among investors, several liquidation cascades, and the overarching bearish price action for most of the year helped explain the OI drop.

A leverage reset can be healthy for the market.

Alongside the weekly BTC chart, there was hope for a bear market bottom. Even so, it remains risky to buy, as a bear market continuation cannot yet be fully ruled out.

#4993. Why Bitcoin surged toward $64,000 before pulling back as trading slows 54% into Thanksgiving

Bitcoin recovered from a weekend low near $55,100 to approach $64,000 before retreating toward $62,500. Earlier Coinbase data showed trading volume falling 54% in a comparable morning hour.

Bitcoin traded near $61,200 early Monday, up 0.5% over 24 hours after falling to approximately $55,100 early Saturday. The recovery subsequently accelerated as U.S. markets reopened, carrying Bitcoin toward $64,000 before a volatile pullback toward $62,500. Wednesday's U.S. inflation report and fresh ETF flow data will provide further tests of the rebound.

Bitcoin had already reclaimed $61,000 on Sunday. Through Monday’s morning reading, about $4.65 billion changed hands in 24 hours across the spot markets CoinGlass tracks, where investors trade Bitcoin directly. That was about 24% less than in the previous 24 hours.

The Coinbase trading data showed a sharper slowdown in one comparable hour. About 333 bitcoin changed hands against the dollar from 7 to 8 a.m. ET Monday, compared with about 730 in the same hour Sunday. That is a decline of about 54%. Bitcoin ended the Monday hour at $61,253 on CryptoSlate's Bitcoin price page.

From 7 to 8 a.m. ET, 729.99 BTC traded Sunday and 333.38 BTC Monday in Coinbase Exchange’s dollar market.

Source: Coinbase Exchange hourly candles · · Coinbase candle field definitions

Bitcoin extended its recovery during Monday's U.S. session, climbing from about $61,200 earlier in the day toward $64,000 after NVIDIA announced Jensen Huang's return, before retreating toward $62,500.

The rally briefly put Bitcoin approximately 16% above Saturday's low near $55,100. Even after the pullback, the cryptocurrency remained approximately 13% above that weekend trough.

The volatile price action followed an earlier slowdown in spot trading. Coinbase recorded approximately 333 BTC changing hands against the dollar during the comparable morning hour Monday, down 54% from Sunday's 730 BTC.

That comparison captures trading conditions before the subsequent rally. The later advance and reversal add a new development to the recovery, while leaving open whether trading activity strengthened as U.S. investors returned.

The next U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flow figures will provide another measure of demand. Farside Investors' latest completed tally had shown $669 million in net outflows on Friday, before the weekend rebound.

Stocks were coming off a rough Friday. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% in that session, and futures tracking the index were up 2.1% early Monday before the U.S. stock market opened, according to Libella’s morning market update. Around 7 a.m. London time, the same report put Brent crude futures near $90 a barrel, gold futures up about 3% and the U.S. dollar index down about 0.2%.

A separate test comes from funds that hold Bitcoin and trade on stock exchanges. Farside Investors’ flow data showed $669.2 million in net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs on Friday, the latest completed tally available Monday morning. The next full report will show whether investors continued withdrawing money from the funds or returned as Bitcoin recovered. A cryptocurrency can rise through the weekend while its U.S. exchange-listed funds are out of session, so the next tally will put a different group of market participants into view.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis has scheduled two reports for 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday. One includes the October personal consumption expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. The other updates the estimate of third-quarter economic growth. In September, consumer prices measured by PCE rose 3.6% from a year earlier. Excluding food and energy, they rose 3.1%.

An inflation reading above expectations could keep interest-rate expectations elevated and make it harder for Bitcoin’s rebound to extend. A softer reading could give it room if Treasury yields ease. With the growth and inflation reports due together, yields and the dollar can help put Bitcoin’s first price move in context. The Fed’s Beige Book comes out at 2 p.m. ET, offering a look at business conditions across the country.

NYSE markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday’s main stock session ends at 1 p.m. ET. Bitcoin exchanges can keep trading through the holiday. Spot Bitcoin ETFs listed on NYSE Arca skip Thursday’s regular session, so Bitcoin can move during a stretch when the funds’ main market is closed. For Arca, the gap runs from 4 p.m. ET Wednesday to 9:30 a.m. ET Friday. A Bitcoin price move during that stretch can carry through to the next regular session for fund holders. Friday’s shortened session leaves less regular trading time for the funds to respond to any holiday moves.

#4992. US Strikes Back After $6 Billion Binance Hack

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

As per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ said that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

The recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

The DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

The importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

“North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva said.

U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities quickly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

The U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

"The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," said Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

Is THIS dip a good time to invest? One analyst thinks so.

Bitcoin’s Fear & Greed Index stood at 11, compared to 50 in early November, reflecting a sharp shift in market sentiment alongside BTC’s 20% correction.  Long-term investors may benefit from this as many weak holders are offloading their BTC. This allows large investors to take up the BTC on sale, allowing them to buy it cheaper.

Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s recent post showing his famous Bitcoin buying signal suggests whales may be getting into the market.

With BTC falling toward $56k, extreme fear, and Strategy’s continued purchases, it does lend some support to the analyst’s view that this dip could be a buying opportunity.

But the bigger question remains: Does buying the dip offer enough long-term upside?

In terms of on-chain and technical indicators, BTC has seen a 40% pullback from its post-election rally in 2024. From a long-term perspective, it has also pulled back to levels seen 5 years prior.

This means Bitcoin has erased years of price gains, raising questions about whether the recent correction can be viewed as a buying opportunity or if it is indicative of a deeper market downturn.

Simply put, does Bitcoin’s long-term return profile justify Michael Saylor’s latest purchase and analysts’ bullish outlook? Or could weakening returns and a prolonged price decline discourage smart money from accumulating Bitcoin [BTC]?

Key onchain signals are already showing a divergence from the analysts’ bullish outlook.

While there is extreme fear in the market, a whale moved 2,279 BTC into Binance, while another whale took a 40x BTC short worth $91 million.

Extreme fear has historically attracted bargain hunters. However, these whale transactions suggested some large investors were preparing for further downside.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s supply distribution painted an equally concerning picture. Nearly 57% of BTC’s supply was sitting at a loss, leaving just 43% in profit.

However, large players are taking a more risk-averse stance, making the possibility of further capitulation harder to ignore.

Ultimately, extreme fear alone may not be enough to confirm a bottom. This puts Saylor’s latest Bitcoin buy signal in a different light.

With BTC’s long-term structure weakening, limited signs of whale accumulation, and capitulation risks rising, buying the dip may carry more downside risk than potential upside.

Extreme fear and Strategy’s continued Bitcoin purchases suggest a potential buying opportunity, but they do not confirm a market bottom.

Rising supply in loss, whale selling, and large short positions point to further downside and capitulation risks.

#4989. More than $2 billion rushed out of Sky’s stablecoin in a single day

Sky Frontier Foundation says holders swapped more than $2 billion of USDS for USDC at par on Nov. 19. The shared USDC reserve fell by about 1.69 billion USDC before an Obex repayment helped refill it.

Holders swapped more than $2 billion of Sky’s USDS for USDC on Nov. 19, according to Sky Frontier Foundation. Sky’s Ethereum reserve for one-for-one swaps fell by about two-thirds in hours. At 17:55 UTC it held 867 million USDC, the amount immediately available to USDS and DAI holders using the shared pool. Seconds later, a debt repayment in Sky’s Obex allocation vault put about 100 million USDC back into the pool.

The foundation said its Peg Stability Module kept exchanging USDS for USDC at one-for-one throughout the day. The reported $2 billion-plus was gross volume in that direction.

The reserve fell from 2.56 billion USDC earlier on Nov. 19 to 867 million USDC before the Obex repayment, a net decline of 1.69 billion USDC. The foundation’s gross figure counts trades in one direction. The balance change reflects USDC moving both ways.

The foundation said the reserve stayed at or above 800 million USDC and later crossed 1.1 billion on Nov. 20. The 867 million reading comes from Ethereum block 26450759, 24 seconds before the Obex repayment. At 12:38 UTC on Nov. 23, Sky’s PSM dashboard showed 1.76 billion USDC, just over twice the pre-repayment balance.

The reserve fell to 867 million USDC shortly before 17:56 UTC on Nov. 19. Four on-chain balances show the drawdown and partial recovery.

Source: Early Nov. 19 · 17:41 balance · Pre-refill balance · 17:41 block · Transfer records · 19:10 balance · Nov. 20 balance

Sky’s LitePSM guide explains how the Ethereum module serves both tokens. A DAI holder can trade directly. For a USDS holder, a separate contract converts USDS to DAI inside the same transaction and pays out USDC from the same reserve. The module keeps those USDC tokens at a separate address called the pocket.

At 15:48 UTC on Nov. 19, a holder exchanged 400 million USDS for 400 million USDC. The USDS was burned, the equivalent amount of DAI went into the module, and the pocket sent the holder USDC.

That shared inventory sets a ceiling for both tokens. A holder can take out only as much USDC as is available when the trade executes. Other swaps can change that amount within the same block. Governance can set fees or pause either direction. The one-for-one rate describes trades through the module itself. Sky has also integrated USDS and USDC routing with Uniswap, where Uniswap swap fees can depend on the route. Holders who want bank dollars after the exchange still need a separate USDC redemption route.

#4988. Hong Kong pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules

Hong Kong’s securities regulator says the proposal would strengthen investor protections, with the bill set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration, extending oversight beyond trading platforms.

On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing to regulate four activities, including virtual asset dealing, advisory, management and custody. Firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from or register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The proposed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would subject providers to fit-and-proper checks and other regulatory requirements. Banks and stored-value facility licensees supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also have to register with the SFC to offer virtual asset services.

SFC chief executive Julia Leung said the proposal would strengthen investor protections and provide clearer paths for responsible innovation. The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

In October, Hong Kong said it would introduce legislation covering those four activities before the end of 2026, following consultations on the proposed framework.

The expanded regime has raised implementation concerns. In January, the Hong Kong Securities & Futures Professionals Association warned that introducing licenses without transitional arrangements could force existing businesses to suspend operations while their applications are reviewed. The association called for a six- to 12-month grace period.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP ETF Shares Surface in Schwab’s Repo Collateral

XRP ETF shares just appeared in collateral baskets pledged by JPMorgan & Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund.

XRP exchange-traded fund shares appeared in collateral baskets posted by JPMorgan and Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund, according to wealth coach Kamilah Stevenson.

In her latest YouTube episode, she argues that the reported holdings point to a less visible source of institutional demand: securities pledged against loans rather than bought for price exposure.

The distinction matters. Stevenson says Schwab did not buy XRP or the ETFs outright; its fund lent cash and received baskets of securities backing the transactions.

Citing monthly SEC disclosures, Stevenson identifies XRP ETF shares from Grayscale, Canary, Franklin and Bitwise among collateral supplied by the banks’ trading arms.

She puts their combined value at roughly $36,000 in April, $2 million in June and more than $8 million by August, an increase exceeding 200-fold.

Those figures remain claims presented in the video. The transcript does not specify the reporting year or filing identifiers, limiting verification of the sequence.

Stevenson acknowledges that the positions were small relative to the underlying loans. Their inclusion would demonstrate acceptance of particular ETF securities within collateral baskets, not necessarily an institutional commitment to holding XRP directly.

The YouTube video episode connects those reported positions to BlackRock’s effort to expand acceptance of tokenized fund shares as collateral. Dr. Stevenson says the appeal is straightforward: investors could pledge income-producing fund shares instead of redeeming them to provide cash.

She also points to Binance’s acceptance of BlackRock’s BUIDL fund as collateral and describes a wider shift toward blockchain-based collateral transfers. Her thesis is that assets used to secure financing can generate more persistent demand than assets held solely for trading.

“Trading creates excitement; collateral creates demand that stays,” Dr. Stevenson says.

That argument needs a boundary. Acceptance of XRP ETF shares does not establish that lenders accept XRP itself, and tokenized collateral does not automatically require XRP to move between markets. Stevenson presents direct XRP-backed lending and cross-currency settlement as potential next steps, not completed developments.

NVIDIA added about $1 trillion in market value on Nov. 23 as its shares surged more than 35% after the unexpected reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

The gains followed NVIDIA's announcement that its board had unanimously reinstated Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.

Directors said discussions with Huang had satisfied them about his ability to lead the company. The board also consulted senior US government officials before concluding that his reinstatement posed no national security risk.

The decision reversed NVIDIA's Nov. 12 leadership shake-up, which had intensified selling across technology stocks and cryptocurrencies.

The rebound extended beyond NVIDIA, with the Nasdaq advancing more than 6% and the S&P 500 gaining approximately 5% in early trading.

The analytics firm observed the rally spread from altcoins to the Nasdaq and Bitcoin, while the S&P 500 posted a smaller advance.

The rapid rotation showed how quickly appetite for speculative assets returned following the leadership reversal at the world's leading AI chipmaker.

The reinstatement also produced a dramatic reversal in prediction-market pricing.

On Nov. 16, CryptoSlate previously reported that Polymarket traders assigned Huang only a 6% probability of returning to NVIDIA by Nov. 30, despite growing pressure from prominent technology executives and investors.

At the time, the probability of a return by Dec. 31 stood at 14%, while the longer-dated contract covering December 2027 carried a 38% probability.

However, those expectations changed significantly following NVIDIA's announcement. By Nov. 23, the November contract had climbed to 99.3%, before reaching 100% on Polymarket's market page.

#4981. Robinhood Chain pays Ethereum 70% more than Base despite collecting 64% less in fees

New data reveals a sharp settlement cost disparity between the two layer-2 networks, even as both retain more than 97% of user fees after Ethereum expenses.

Robinhood Chain paid Ethereum 70% more than Coinbase-backed Base to settle transactions, even though it collected 64% fewer user fees over 30 days.

The network spent approximately $25,700 on Ethereum settlement costs between Oct. 23 and Nov. 21, compared with Base's $15,100, according to Castle Labs data compiled from growthepie.

However, Base generated $2.97 million in transaction fees over the same period, nearly three times Robinhood Chain's $1.07 million.

That disparity left Robinhood Chain spending $2.41 on Ethereum settlement for every $100 collected from users, compared with just 51 cents for Base.

The figures expose a significant difference in the networks' settlement costs, even as both retain the overwhelming majority of transaction fees after paying Ethereum.

The gap is particularly striking because Base consumed considerably more Ethereum data capacity.

According to Blobscan data, Base posted approximately 350,000 blobs during the period, nearly twice Robinhood Chain's 182,000. Blobs let Ethereum's layer-2 networks publish transaction data at lower cost.

Base consequently spent about $4,478 on blob fees, compared with Robinhood Chain's $2,315.

However, the remaining settlement costs tell a different story. Excluding blob fees, Robinhood Chain spent approximately $23,379, more than double Base's $10,602.

Those additional expenses include standard Ethereum transaction fees for posting data and updating settlement states.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Settlement and data-posting costs in USD. Labels show the UTC start dates of four seven-day periods in 2026. The article covers Nov. 20 and 21 separately.

Source: growthepie Robinhood Chain daily settlement fees · growthepie Base daily settlement fees

The comparison highlights a broader imbalance in Ethereum's scaling economy, where layer-2 networks collect transaction fees while paying relatively little to the blockchain securing their operations.

Across all tracked Ethereum layer-2 networks, users paid approximately $5 million in fees during the 30 days ending Nov. 21, while the networks paid Ethereum just $74,500 for settlement and data availability.

That represents roughly 1.5% of user fees, leaving approximately 98.5% after Ethereum settlement expenses, before accounting for other operating and revenue-sharing costs.

Base and Robinhood Chain accounted for about $4.04 million of those combined fees but paid Ethereum only $40,800.

The difference reflects how Ethereum's scaling architecture distributes economic activity. Layer-2 networks handle user transactions and collect their associated fees, while Ethereum provides settlement and data availability for a comparatively small charge.

For Ethereum, the resulting payments contribute to transaction fee burning and validator income, but remain modest relative to the economic activity taking place on its scaling networks.

The November figures raise two questions: whether Robinhood Chain can narrow its settlement-cost disadvantage against Base, and how much additional revenue Ethereum can capture as layer-2 networks continue handling most user activity.

#4980. Trump to host second memecoin dinner tonight with TRUMP down 99% from peak

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

One holder nabbed a seat with only $518 worth of TRUMP, a huge drop from the roughly $55,000 worth that holders required for the first dinner in May 2025, according to The Washington Post.

President Donald Trump is set to host a dinner on Sunday night for the largest holders of his Official Trump Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin at Trump National Golf Club in Northern Virginia, outside Washington, according to the event's website. It is the second dinner and the third event overall for top TRUMP holders since the token launched in January 2025.

Fight Fight Fight LLC, the firm that promotes the memecoin, invited the top 185 holders based on their average TRUMP holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 16. One holder reached No. 179 after buying just $518 worth of TRUMP in October and November, according to a Washington Post analysis published Wednesday. It took at least $55,000 worth of the token to qualify for the first dinner, the Post found.

The Post's analysis also found more than 5,000 holders who could have qualified by registering but did not, even after organizers extended sign-ups by four days.

The top 29 holders are invited to a VIP reception with Trump and one of the event's celebrity guests, and the top 120 will receive gift bags that include a Trump watch, Trump fragrance, and a commemorative ticket and poster, according to the site. The top four VIP holders will also get 18-karat gold Trump watches, provided they hold at least 1 million TRUMP, a stake worth about $895,000 at Sunday's price.

Boxer Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson are scheduled to appear, along with mentalist Lior Suchard, according to the site. The site says there will be no private meetings with the president and that no gifts will be accepted.

TRUMP traded at $0.8950 on Sunday, down 98.8% from its all-time high of $73.43 in January 2025, just after the token launched, according to The Block's Official Trump price page. In the two weeks after this dinner was announced, TRUMP's trading volume fell about 35% and its price dropped 9%, according to Kaiko data cited by Bloomberg. Volume rose to between four and eight times its prior levels after each of the first two events were announced, Kaiko found.

Singapore-linked trading platform FastX, which reached the top of the holder leaderboard for the event, said on X on Thursday that it will attend the dinner "as an independent holder" and bring 10 questions chosen by a vote of its community. FastX has said it is not affiliated with Trump or the TRUMP project.

Morten Christensen, founder of crypto giveaways site Airdrop Alert, also plans to attend, the company said on X. Christensen, who attended both earlier events and qualified for the VIP reception, told The Wall Street Journal he bought 75,000 TRUMP at an average price of $1.70 while shorting a roughly equal amount through perpetual futures on Hyperliquid.

By holding the token and betting on its decline in price, Christensen came away with a profit of about $6, he said, due to funding fees. The same approach cost him about $1,200 for the first event and $500 for the second, he told Bloomberg. He used the same approach to win a seat for his sister.

Tron founder Justin Sun, who was the largest TRUMP holder at the May 2025 dinner, is not attending, the Journal reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Sun sued World Liberty Financial, the Trump family's crypto venture, which operates independently of the memecoin, in April, accusing it of freezing his WLFI tokens. World Liberty has called his claims "entirely meritless."

Trump hosted the top 220 holders at the same golf club in May 2025, and the promoter held a conference and luncheon for 297 holders at Mar-a-Lago in April. Trump has not posted about the dinner or the memecoin on social media this year, per the Post. The scoring window for the promoter's next contest, a three-day Super Bowl LXI package in Los Angeles for the top 18 holders, opens on Sunday, according to the site.

Eight senators led by Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., asked the White House in a letter last month to publish a list of attendees, saying the event "appears to be a pay-to-play scheme." Democrats, who won control of both chambers of Congress in this month's midterms, have pledged to investigate Trump's crypto ventures.

"The President's attendance at a privately organized event does not make it a White House event or government function," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Bloomberg. The White House directed questions about potential conflicts of interest to Fight Fight Fight, which did not respond to Bloomberg's request for comment.

Career staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission opened an inquiry into possible fraud involving TRUMP soon after its launch in early 2025, but backed off after concluding the commission would not approve subpoenas, The New York Times reported Friday, citing three former agency officials with direct knowledge of the inquiry who spoke on condition of anonymity.

The officials were concerned about possible insider trading after some early buyers posted large profits, and believed then-acting Chair Caroline Pham would not sign off, according to the Times. The inquiry did not get far enough to determine whether any wrongdoing occurred, and a CFTC spokeswoman declined to comment.

Trump collected at least $636 million in transaction and licensing fees from the memecoin last year, according to his financial disclosures, while nearly a million buyers lost a combined $3.81 billion through the end of June, according to Nansen data cited by The New York Times.

#4979. Monad faces $190 million insider token unlock larger than its market cap as MON hits record low

The 16.61 billion MON release equals 140.5% of circulating supply, threatening fresh selling pressure and a potential shake-up in validator voting power.

Monad is preparing to unlock 16.61 billion MON tokens on Nov. 24, exceeding its circulating supply as the cryptocurrency hits record lows.

The release represents 140.5% of the 11.83 billion MON currently circulating and marks the first major insider distribution since the blockchain launched in November 2025.

According to DefiLlama, approximately 10.7 billion MON will go to team members, 4.925 billion to investors, and 987.5 million to the Category Labs treasury. This means its team and investor allocations account for 94% of the release.

The unlock was valued at approximately $226 million in Tokenomist's earlier estimate, but MON's decline has reduced its value to roughly $190 million, still exceeding the token's $137 million market capitalization.

CryptoSlate's data shows MON plunged around 11% over the past 24 hours, touching an all-time low of $0.01152 ahead of the release. It is trading at $0.012 as of press time.

The incoming supply adds to existing market pressure, with further insider distributions scheduled through 2029.

Historical data from Alea Research shows that 16 comparable token unlocks recorded median declines of 25.2% in the preceding month and 6.9% in the following month.

Category Labs has authorized up to $80 million in MON repurchases through Dec. 31, although Alea found no disclosed purchases under the program.

Beyond potential selling, the release could alter how Monad distributes voting power and staking rewards.

The network had 20.73 billion MON backing validator votes across 197 operators on Nov. 22, according to Valopers.

If insiders stake just 2.3 billion MON, approximately 14% of their newly available allocation, those tokens would account for 10% of the resulting voting power, assuming existing stake remains unchanged.

At 25% participation, approximately 4.15 billion MON would enter active staking, representing 16.7% of the expanded total.

That scenario would also reduce gross inflationary rewards per staked MON by 16.7%, assuming issuance and validator commissions remain constant.

#4978. A $2 million exploit leads to a $3.7 million free-for-all as traders empty Fusionist’s ACE bridge

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

A hacker minted quintillions of fake ACE tokens on BNB Chain and sold them for $2 million, crashing the price. Traders then bought the cheap tokens and swapped them for real ACE worth $3.7 million.

An attacker made off with about $2 million on Sunday by minting a massive quantity of unbacked ACE Fusionist (ACE) tokens, a creation of blockchain game project Fusionist, on BNB Chain and selling them for USDT while crashing ACE's price on the network, according to The Block's analysis of onchain data.

Traders then took the same cheap tokens, which by then numbered in the billions, and sent them through Fusionist's bridge, emptying it of its 53.7 million real ACE, worth about $3.7 million at current prices, onchain data shows. ACE's circulating supply before the exploit was only around 116 million tokens.

Fusionist is a blockchain gaming studio backed by Binance Labs (now YZi Labs) that makes sci-fi strategy games and runs its own blockchain, Endurance. ACE is the project's native token, which is used to pay transaction fees on Endurance. It trades on exchanges including Binance and OKX. A copy of the ACE token also exists as a separate token on BNB Chain. Fusionist runs a bridge that converts ACE between the two blockchains.

Onchain analytics account Onchain Lens said on X that the attacker "exploited Fusionist's privileged bridge-minter access" to mint unbacked ACE and swap it for USDT, then routed $1.87 million through crypto mixer Tornado Cash. The Block traced about 1,150 ETH, worth roughly $2 million, into Tornado Cash from wallets that either received the minted ACE directly from the bridge or collected proceeds from its sale. The attacker moved the funds from BNB Chain to Ethereum through cross-chain swap services including SwftSwap and Relay.

The first mint, of 3.5 million ACE, came at 12:55 p.m. ET, according to BscScan data. ACE has a maximum supply of 147 million tokens. The mints grew to billions, then trillions, then quadrillions of ACE over the next two and a half hours, ending with a 10 quintillion ACE mint at 3:28 p.m.

The mints were sent from a wallet that Fusionist's deployer funded nearly three years ago, BscScan data shows. Blockchain security firm Blockaid, which first flagged the exploit, listed that wallet among the exploiter addresses.

The attacker sold each batch into decentralized exchange pools on BNB Chain as soon as it was minted. By 1:41 p.m. ET, one trader was able to buy ACE there for about $0.0001, compared with the roughly $0.04 price of ACE on exchanges at the time.

Fusionist's bridge holds ACE tokens on its Endurance network to back the tokens on BNB Chain. When a user sends BNB Chain ACE back to the bridge, it burns those tokens and releases the same amount of ACE on Endurance. The bridge kept working after the attack, so any trader could buy the crashed tokens on BNB Chain and swap them for real ACE tokens, then sell them on exchanges.

From 1:13 p.m. to 3:05 p.m. ET, the Endurance contract paid out about 53.7 million ACE to 24 addresses, according to Endurance block explorer data. One address alone received 26.1 million, nearly a quarter of ACE's former circulating supply.

The bridge held about 53.7 million ACE before the hack; by Sunday afternoon it held only 0.08 ACE. Another 27 attempted transfers, totaling roughly 1.36 billion ACE, failed because the bridge was already nearly empty by that point.

Pseudonymous X user ZAMA_APPLE was the first to post about a user exploiting the arbitrage, sharing a screenshot that showed a trader turning $60 into $17,000 by buying ACE on BNB Chain and selling it on OKX. The Block traced the trade to a single wallet.

The wallet started with about $50 in USDT, withdrawn from Binance around 1:34 p.m. ET. It spent $10 testing the bridge, then used its remaining $40 to buy about 404,000 ACE at 1:41 p.m. Four minutes later, the bridge paid out the same amount of real ACE on Endurance, and the trader sent it straight to the exchange. By 1:53 p.m., it had sold the tokens for about $17,670, a 350x return.

Fusionist told its followers at 2:30 p.m. ET to pause ACE transfers, trades and bridging on BSC while it investigates "an apparent ongoing exploit." Fusionist has not posted an update since, as of publication time.

Crypto exchange Gate said its security team confirmed the bridge was exploited and that it would roll back all ACE/USDT trades executed between 12:55 p.m. and 2:15 p.m. ET. Gate also switched its ACE perpetual futures market to reduce-only and said it would settle and delist the market late Monday.

Some Gate users who sold ACE during that window were left with negative balances after Gate rolled back their trades, returning their ACE and reclaiming the USDT from the sales, Gate's support account said on X.

ACE is down about 20% over the past 24 hours, trading at roughly $0.069, according to The Block's price page. The Block has reached out to Fusionist and OKX for comment.

#4977. US lawmakers propose up to 30% rewards for prediction market whistleblowers

Whistleblowers could receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases exceeding $1 million in penalties.

Two US lawmakers have proposed paying whistleblowers up to 30% of monetary sanctions in qualifying prediction market fraud cases, seeking tips about suspected insider trading.

On Friday, Democratic Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu announced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026. The bill would establish a Department of Justice program rewarding people whose original information helps resolve enforcement actions.

Under the proposal, whistleblowers would receive 10% to 30% of monetary sanctions from covered federal fraud cases involving prediction market platforms, provided that the sanctions exceed $1 million. The rewards would come from the DOJ’s Assets Forfeiture Fund, with the Attorney General determining payouts based on the significance of information and assistance.

The bill would permit anonymous submissions through lawyers and prohibit employer retaliation against whistleblowers.

The lawmakers cited concerns about government insiders profiting from bets on military operations and presidential speeches, including on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.

The latest proposal follows Senate passage of the DEATH BETS Act on Thursday, which would prohibit federally regulated prediction markets from offering contracts tied to war, assassination, terrorism and death.

In March, lawmakers introduced separate legislation to prevent officials from using nonpublic information to trade prediction market contracts. In May, House lawmakers sought records from Kalshi and Polymarket over suspected insider trading linked to military actions.
